scope: Bench configuration and diagnostics. Physical engine outputs remain inhibited; no vehicle qualification.
general: Board pin numbers refer to the PCB top view; pin 1 is the square pad. The mating plug view can be mirrored. Verify the actual harness with continuity tests.
Disconnect power before resistance/continuity tests. Do not measure resistance on a live vehicle bus or use a megohmmeter on electronics.
Keep J3 open and all actuator harnesses disconnected during sensor commissioning. This firmware keeps ARM off.
Use the actual sensor or controller manufacturer pinout, transfer curve, mounting torque and air gap. There is no universal vehicle-side pinout.
Measure signal voltage against that sensor connector pin 1, not an arbitrary chassis bolt. Never use a test lamp on a sensor or MCU pin.

sensors.name: MAP / manifold pressure
mount: Retain the OEM pressure port or use a suitable sealed manifold-pressure takeoff after the throttle. Keep the hose short and secure, and follow the sensor maker's fluid/orientation limits.
Route away from hot exhaust and ignition wiring. Leak-check any added hose before running an engine.
checks: Confirm the sensor uses 5 V and identify its actual supply, ground and signal wires from its datasheet.
With power off, check each harness conductor end-to-end and for unintended shorts, with both ends unplugged.
Power the board, check pin 2 near 5 V, then connect the sensor and measure pin 3 versus pin 1.
Use a regulated hand vacuum/pressure source within the sensor rating, compare the web voltage with a meter, then enter the manufacturer transfer curve or measured reference points.
expected: Key-on / engine-off pressure should agree with a trusted local absolute-pressure reference after calibration. It is not always 100 kPa.
A steady applied pressure should produce a steady voltage and calibrated value.
faults: Flat near 0 V: inspect power, ground, signal short and sensor pin order.
Flat high: inspect a short to supply, wrong curve, or a saturated sensor.
Pressure wrong but voltage agrees with the meter: check absolute versus gauge units, curve and pressure reference.
Noisy or slow: inspect hose leaks/restriction, ground offset, shield routing and configured filtering.
sensors.circuit: R20 22k series, R21 33k to ground, C20 10nF; U6 channel 0.

sensors.name: TPS / throttle position
mount: Use the OEM TPS mounting and its correct shaft coupling. A single analog input does not replace an electronic throttle system or its redundant safety channels.
Turn the throttle only with the vehicle made safe; do not force an electronic throttle plate or alter mechanical stops.
checks: Identify whether the TPS is a 3-wire potentiometer or another sensor. Do not connect throttle-motor wires to J12.
Verify pin 2 supply and pin 1 ground, then observe signal voltage while moving the permitted mechanism slowly.
Record closed and fully open reference voltages, enter those as 0% and 100%, and mark calibration confirmed only after checking the whole travel.
expected: The voltage should sweep smoothly without dropouts. Some sensors have a decreasing transfer curve; configure the corresponding endpoint values.
faults: Jumps at one position: inspect sensor track/coupling or a broken harness conductor.
Direction reversed: swap calibration endpoint values, not supply and ground wires.
Does not reach 0%/100%: recheck mechanical travel and measured endpoints.
Two TPS tracks or a throttle motor are present: this hardware does not implement OEM DBW control.
sensors.circuit: R22 22k series, R23 33k to ground, C21 10nF; U6 channel 1.

sensors.name: Coolant temperature
mount: Use the OEM coolant sensor and mounting boss, with the engine cold and cooling system depressurized. Follow the specified seal and torque.
Keep the original vehicle sensor if required by other systems; verify loading before sharing any signal.
checks: For a passive two-wire NTC, use pins 1 and 3 only. Leave pin 2 empty in the mating housing.
Fit R32 only if this is a passive NTC requiring the board pull-up. Check its actual resistance; the design value is 2.49 kohm.
Measure sensor resistance while disconnected and compare at known temperatures with its datasheet. Prefer several reference points.
Enter beta parameters or a voltage table. In NTC mode, confirm the physical pull-up is fitted; the UI cannot install a resistor.
expected: A common NTC resistance falls as temperature rises, and its signal voltage falls with this pull-up topology.
The conversion accounts for the board's 55 kohm divider load and measured sensor supply.
faults: Near 0 V: sensor/loom short to ground or very low resistance.
High signal / open-model fault: unplugged sensor, broken ground/signal or missing/wrong pull-up.
Plausible voltage but wrong temperature: wrong NTC curve, pull-up value, supply reading or units.
Do not assume a floating/unexcited input will read maximum voltage: R32 is DNP by default.
sensors.circuit: R24 22k series, R25 33k to ground, C22 10nF; U6 channel 2.

sensors.name: Intake-air temperature
mount: Use a suitable intake-air boss and the sensor maker's orientation. Avoid placing the sensing element against the intake wall or at an unrepresentative heat source.
Follow the original mechanical arrangement; secure any aftermarket sensor so it cannot enter the intake.
checks: A passive two-wire NTC connects to pins 1 and 3; pin 2 remains empty.
R33 is the optional board pull-up, normally 2.49 kohm. Confirm it is physically fitted before using NTC conversion.
Compare disconnected resistance and stabilized readings with a reference thermometer at several temperatures. Enter the actual sensor curve.
expected: After a long cold soak, intake and coolant temperature should be reasonably consistent with their actual surroundings. Heat soak can produce real differences.
faults: Use the same open/short/pull-up checks as CLT, but inspect intake heat soak and airflow before blaming calibration.
Fast spikes suggest intermittent wires or electrical interference. A slow heat-soak drift may be physical.
sensors.circuit: R26 22k series, R27 33k to ground, C23 10nF; U6 channel 3.

sensors.name: Wideband controller output
mount: Install the exhaust sensor according to the sensor/controller maker's rules for bung angle, temperature and condensation. The ECU board does not heat or drive a raw wideband sensor.
Mount the external controller away from hot exhaust and splash paths; use its specified fused power and grounds.
checks: Connect controller analog signal to pin 3 and its specified analog reference to pin 1.
Leave pin 2 unpopulated; the board sensor supply must not power the controller or heater.
Enter the controller's actual 0-5 V mapping and units. Lambda and AFR are not interchangeable without the correct fuel stoichiometry.
Use the controller's documented analog-output test mode or a known voltage source before interpreting exhaust readings.
expected: Web voltage and a meter should agree; converted lambda should agree with the controller when both use the same mapping and ground reference.
faults: Controller display correct but ECU wrong: inspect mapping, analog-reference offset and output mode.
Fixed fault voltage: read the external controller's error codes before treating it as mixture.
No output until heated: verify controller state and heater supply.
A raw LSU sensor cannot be connected directly; do not invent a direct 5-wire/6-wire pin mapping.
sensors.circuit: R28 22k series, R29 33k to ground, C24 10nF; U6 channel 4.

sensors.name: Buffered post-catalyst signal
mount: Retain the catalyst and rear oxygen sensor in their proper locations. This input is for measurement, not catalyst emulation or bypass.
Use a suitable external high-input-impedance conditioner/buffer where needed. The board input presents about 55 kohm to the sensor signal.
checks: Connect only the buffer's conditioned 0-5 V output to pin 3 and its analog reference to pin 1. Leave pin 2 empty unless the buffer specifically permits this supply within the shared current budget.
Do not connect heater wires, a raw wideband sensor, or assume every raw narrowband output can tolerate this load.
Compare the buffer output with a meter; enter its transfer curve or retain voltage display.

Optional engine EMAP or baro role: disconnect the postcat buffer and assign J16 in Engine development. Connect one suitable absolute-pressure sensor: pin 1 ground, pin 2 protected 5 V only if its supply specification permits, pin 3 conditioned 0-5 V output. Do not parallel two signals.

Calibrate the postcat channel in exact unit kPa using a measured linear or table conversion, then confirm it. EMAP requires20..500 kPa absolute; baro requires50..110 kPa absolute. The about55 kohm input load and shared supply/current budget still apply. A voltage reading with a kPa label is not a pressure calibration.
expected: Voltage is the directly supported diagnostic. This firmware does not implement catalyst-efficiency monitoring, emissions readiness or OEM rear-sensor diagnostics.

The default engine role is postcat_monitor. An explicit EMAP or live baro assignment reuses this existing protected ADC channel, with no extra simultaneous channel. EMAP plus live baro requires an additional input path that is not implemented. No zero-RPM ambient capture is inferred.

Keep an exhaust-pressure transducer within its temperature rating with appropriate remote tubing. Pressure/thermal installation remains unqualified. Engine status, recorded logs and own008 tuning diagnostics identify the selected source, pressure normalization and unknown readings. Physical outputs remain inhibited.
faults: Signal changes when shared with OEM ECU: stop and review input loading and the buffer interface.
Zero or clipped output: inspect buffer supply/reference and output limits.
A stable rear reading alone does not prove catalyst health.
sensors.circuit: R30 22k series, R31 33k to ground, C25 10nF; U6 channel 5.

triggers.name: Crank Hall input
mount: Use the original rigid bracket/target-wheel relationship and the exact manufacturer air gap, polarity, supply rating and torque. There is no universal trigger gap.
This input accepts a compatible 5 V Hall interface. A two-wire variable-reluctance sensor needs an external conditioner.
checks: Verify supply and ground before connecting. Determine whether the Hall output is push-pull or open-collector.
For an open-collector output without another suitable pull-up, fit the specified optional pull-up and verify the current/voltage requirements.
Use an oscilloscope to compare connector pin 3 with the conditioned MCU input. A multimeter can miss missing pulses and noise.
With ignition/injection disabled, turn the target safely or use an isolated bench signal generator. Do not connect a generator in parallel with an energized sensor.
expected: The decoder uses rising edges. Trigger logging records both polarities on separate diagnostic capture channels. Both Hall paths use two Schmitt inversions, preserving the input polarity.

Crank sync requires the selected missing-tooth geometry and repeated valid gaps. Batch/wasted and semi-sequential use crank only. Full sequential requires one rising cam pulse per720 degrees and two repeatable observations; phase loss after acquisition cuts and latches until a supervised stop. Confirm mechanical cylinder1 compression reference independently.
faults: No edges: inspect supply, missing pull-up, wrong sensor type, target gap, signal/ground pin order and U7 conditioning.
Edges but no sync: inspect total slots/missing teeth, speed range, signal quality and electrical noise. A simple square wave is not a valid missing-tooth wheel.
False RPM / overflow: inspect ringing, shield/return routing, gap and pull-up; power-cycle after a latched capture overflow.
triggers.circuit: R40 33k series, C30 100pF, optional R41 2.2k pull-up; U7 -> GPIO8.

services.title: Logic power
checks: Pin 1 is externally fused key-on 12 V; pin 2 is ground. Use the specified external 1 A source fuse.
For first bench checks, unplug every sensor and actuator, keep J3 open, use a 12 V current-limited supply, and check polarity before enabling it.
Measure TP2 VIN_PROT, TP3 5 V, TP4 3V3, then each sensor pin 2. TP2 is after the reverse diode and before the input filter.
Repeated resets can be undervoltage/current limit, a short, wrong part orientation, regulator instability or watchdog timeout. Disconnect external loads one at a time.

services.title: UART / boot / reset
checks: Pins: 1 ground, 2 ECU TX -> adapter RX, 3 ECU RX <- adapter TX, 4 EN, 5 BOOT_N. Use 3.3 V logic, 115200 baud, 8-N-1.
Do not connect an adapter power wire or a powered DevKit USB cable while the carrier supplies the module. For USB programming, remove the module from the carrier.
If silent, check supply and EN, cross TX/RX correctly, verify the A3 build and chosen serial port, then capture the boot log. The existing console tag can still say ecu_a0.
For ROM download mode, hold BOOT_N low during an EN reset, then release it. Do not short EN or BOOT_N to 12 V.

services.title: Physical interlock
checks: Pin 1 is 3V3 and pin 2 is INTERLOCK. Open is the normal state during commissioning.
lock=0 with the contact open is expected. Closing it can allow hardware run gating; do not close it with vehicle actuators connected.
The configuration firmware keeps ARM=0 regardless. Never bypass SAFE_N to make a fault disappear.

services.title: Internal expansion
checks: Pins: ground / 3V3 / SDA / SCL / SAFE_N. This is an internal 3.3 V service bus, not a 12 V sensor connector.
Check pull-ups and idle SDA/SCL near 3V3. A stuck-low line suggests a short, wrong device voltage or a device holding the bus.
No generic external I2C scanner or expansion actuator control is implemented by this release.

services.title: CAN and termination
checks: J7: CANH / CANL / ground / CHASSIS. Keep the pair twisted and verify the network bitrate. Firmware reception is 500 kbit/s listen-only; no OEM decoding is provided.
JP1 open leaves MCP2562 in standby, so ordinary frames will not be received. Close it only on the appropriate supervised bus for normal transceiver reception. Firmware remains listen-only.
JP2 adds onboard 120 ohm termination when closed. Leave it open on an already terminated vehicle network.
With the complete network unpowered, two 120 ohm end terminations normally measure about 60 ohm between CANH and CANL. A removed/unpowered interface alone need not read 60 ohm.
No frames: inspect JP1, bitrate, polarity, grounds, bus activity and termination. A standalone two-node listen-only bench cannot supply missing ACKs for a lone transmitter.

services.title: External relay coils
checks: Pins: MAIN low side / PUMP low side / FAN low side / ground. External fused relay supplies and correctly oriented flyback diodes are required.
Target coil current is at most 150 mA per channel, pending physical tests. Do not connect a fan motor or pump motor directly.
The configuration firmware commands all channels OFF. An inactive relay is expected, not a reason to bypass the inhibit.

With a coil connected to a safe test supply, OFF low-side voltage can be near the external supply, not zero. Driver/tab is electrically live. Actuation tests require a separate qualified dummy-load procedure.

services.title: Injector outputs and power return
checks: J9 pins 1-4 are injector low sides 1-4; pins 5-8 are ground. J19 both pins are the dedicated power return.
Only saturated high-impedance PFI injectors are in scope; 1.2 A/channel is a design target pending tests. No GDI or peak-and-hold driver is provided.
Actuator 12 V is external, fused and relay switched. Never use the sensor ground harness as the injector current return.
All outputs remain OFF in this firmware. Check resistance/continuity only disconnected; do not pulse a fueled engine to troubleshoot wiring.
A high OFF output with an externally powered load is normal. Persistent current with ARM off indicates wrong wiring, a shorted driver or a board fault: disconnect power.

services.title: Smart-coil logic only
checks: Pins 1-4 are active-high 5 V smart-coil commands; pin 5 is ground. They are not ignition-coil primary outputs.
Use only a compatible low-current logic input (design target at most 4 mA). Coil power and power-ground wiring remain external.
The configuration firmware keeps dwell commands OFF. Do not use a test lamp, an ordinary LED without its resistor, or a coil primary as a logic test load.
Changing or interrupting dwell on a real coil can produce a spark. Keep real ignition hardware disconnected during bench configuration.

services.title: Shield and enclosure bond
checks: J20 pins and plated lug H5 are CHASSIS, not normal sensor/actuator current returns. Bond them to the internal lining using the assembly guide.
Check lining/braid continuity with power off. The CHASSIS-to-GND 1 Mohm bleed and 4.7 nF RF capacitor are intentional, not a hard DC ground link.
Keep all bonds inside the water seal and route any external reference conductor through a sealed gland. Do not drill an unsealed shield-stud hole.

services.title: Test points
checks: TP1 ground; TP2 VIN_PROT; TP3 5 V; TP4 3V3; TP5 SAFE_N; TP6 RUN_5V.
With J3 open and monitor firmware, RUN_5V should be low even when supplies are healthy. SAFE_N is an open-drain supervised net, normally pulled near 3V3 when released.
If SAFE_N repeatedly drops, scope it with the supply rails and WDI. Do not defeat the MAX1232 or 3V3 supervisor.
Use a properly referenced or isolated scope arrangement; do not clip an earth-referenced scope ground to an arbitrary live output.

services.title: Isolated idle PWM
checks: Engine development contains idle modes, gains, coolant curves and source/age diagnostics. All shipped builds keep physical idle GPIO writes disabled. A3/A4 and the old manual/ZIP do not contain this new carrier connector.

A5 J21 PH4 maps pin 1 GPIO3/IDLE_CMD, pin 2 RUN_5V, pin 3 carrier 5V, pin 4 carrier GND to IAC-DRAFT2 J1 XH4 pins1 through 4. R154 is the permanent 2.2 kohm carrier bias and stays present with the harness unplugged. Verify the keyed mating view and continuity with power removed.

Two input-side transistor buffers and 6N137 optocouplers separate carrier power/return from actuator logic. Do not bridge these domains with wires, case foil, heatsinks or scope ground clips. This is low-voltage return separation, not certified isolation.

Accessory J2 fixed screw terminal: pin 1 separate externally protected, fused, relay-switched 9-16 V; pin 2 dedicated return. J3 VH2: pin 1 valve positive, pin 2 IAC_LS. Use an actual <=2 A normally closed two-wire continuous-PWM valve; carrier J1 and sensor rails cannot supply it.

IRLZ44NPBF has no current/thermal shutdown or valve feedback. A drain-source short can energize a normal-current coil without clearing a fuse. Provide an independently operable actuator-branch disconnect. Q1 drain tab and U6 regulator-output tab are live at different voltages.

C1-C5, C10, R13 and R14 mount on the back. C4/C10 bypass the driver locally; LOGIC_GND joins ACT_GND only at NT1/Q1 source. Do not add a second return strap. Actual passive parts, trimmed leads, finished TO220 holes, underside height and case clearance require assembly acceptance.

Keep this draft unpowered pending release of the protected branch, exact PDIP driver guarantee, loaded GPIO/RUN/opto timing, minimum 1 us pulse, supervisor brownout, temperature and mounting checks. MCP100 assertion 10 us is typical with no specified maximum. Read actual GPIO3/JTAG eFuses without burns; N16R8 socket/antenna fit remains provisional. The RUN source also feeds carrier R47/R50/R53, Q7 and HCT inputs; measure loaded RUN and MAIN_IN with both boards attached. The Q7 500 uA figure at 10 V/25 C is not a 5 V/full-temperature/fault bound.

Use a current-limited resistor fixture first with proper isolated/differential probes and an independent cutoff. Observe local rail, supervisor, ENA, gate/source, drain and both return currents during startup, reset, RUN/command loss, disconnected inputs and opened returns. Preserve scope protective earth.
Compare proposed duty with separate cycle-latched PWM high time and fault. Synthetic current/opening are model estimates; no physical valve feedback exists. Command0% does not prove valve closure.

services.title: Semi-sequential fuel and wasted COP
checks: This is a software development strategy. Selected web builds keep physical engine outputs OFF. The separate dummy-load bench build has no web service and is not installed here. Keep J3 open and real injector/ignition harnesses disconnected. The unchanged carrier needs four independent injector drivers and four smart-coil logic channels; no extra pair wiring is required.

J9 pins1-4 remain physical injector cylinders1-4; pins5-8 are return. J19 is the dedicated power return. J10 pins1-4 remain physical smart-coil commands1-4, pin5 ground. Check each harness by continuity with both ends unplugged. Never bridge low-side outputs or move two injectors onto one driver.

For firing order1-3-4-2 the scheduled fuel pairs are cylinders1+4 and3+2. Other valid four-cylinder orders derive pairs from order slots1+3 and2+4. Each injector opens once per crank revolution, giving two half-effective-fuel openings per720 degrees. Dead time is added to each opening.

Semi-sequential needs crank synchronization from J17, without compression phase from J18. Its closing reference repeats modulo360 degrees:540 means180 each revolution. The two groups are180 degrees apart. Full sequential alone uses the720-degree cam reference and individual trims; enabled trims must be disabled explicitly before saving a paired mode. Stored trim maps are retained.

After saving, check active strategy separately from unsaved editor settings. Compare executed rising/falling timestamps for both members of each pair, full electrical width, duty, fault cause, revision and source age. Injector low deadlines stay fixed after opening, so changing RPM can move the actual closing angle. A missing cam is expected in this mode; a missing crank must cut. Old latched faults still require stopped/quiet recovery.

Pairs can overlap above50 percent duty. Do not assume lower peak supply/return current. Existing1.2A injector and4mA smart-coil targets remain unqualified; saturated high-impedance PFI only. Actual flow/deadtime, current/flyback, loaded supply/gates, timing/jitter, temperature and engine phase need physical dummy-load/HIL acceptance.

The host reduced and research plants have fixed physical1-3-4-2 geometry. Changing the tune order does not change that engine. Coupled comparison uses a neutral test tune, not a vehicle calibration. Screen engine schema2 is required for this mode; schema1 peers fall back to sensors and show upgrade needed.

services.title: MAP/TPS transient acquisition and dose
checks: Use Engine development > Transient fueling. Older tunes retain Legacy TPS decay; Off, TPS rate table and MAP rate table are explicit choices. Selected web images inhibit physical outputs. No new connector or PCB route is required.

J11 is protected MAP and J12 is protected TPS. Reference each signal to its connector pin1 ground and verify the actual sensor supply, mating pinout and calibrated kPa or percent. Do not infer wiring from the sensor body color.

New modes use nominal5ms fast calibrated acquisitions and the scan-start timestamp, independently of display smoothing. Compare raw voltage, calibrated values, window length, source rate, threshold/minimum-change gates and phase/reason. Bad wiring and noise can trigger enrichment.

Extra curve values are percentages. Multiply scales effective current fuel. Add reference fuel uses per-cylinder720-degree mass at100kPa,25C,100%VE and lambda1, independent of current MAP/VE/warmup. Trims scale the complete dose; opening count and deadtime follow.

Deceleration is fuel remaining:100% neutral,0% stops new injector starts after scheduler acceptance while spark continues unless another cut applies. Existing active closing edges finish normally. Dose/pulse/duty limits still inhibit the whole command.

First observation and recovery after stop/crank/fault/DFCO clear history. Rate-valid differs from observation available. Check source age: hold remaining is measured at the observation time. Completed host runs are synthetic and retained logs are historical.
Use engine MSL004 or JSON for detailed transient rates, phase and dose. Fixed ESP-NOW schema2 retains the existing effective accel ratio only. No physical measurement or vehicle base tune is implied.

config_help: Voltage mode shows the reconstructed connector voltage; it does not require a sensor transfer curve.
Linear mode uses two measured input voltages and two physical values. Set the actual units and validate a third reference point.
Table mode interpolates between 2-16 ascending voltage/value pairs. Values outside the table range are faults, not extrapolated measurements.

NTC beta mode is for CLT/IAT only and requires the physical pull-up. It uses the measured sensor supply and compensates the 55 kohm divider load. A voltage table is preferable when the real curve is available.
Filtering is for readout smoothing, not a substitute for fixing wiring/noise. Electrical fault checks use the instantaneous input.
Saved calibration feeds readouts and shadow engine calculations. Physical engine outputs remain inhibited. DBW, catalyst diagnostics and OEM protocols are not implemented.

Saving trigger geometry or engine timing fences virtual output plans and requires fresh synchronization. Batch and semi-sequential use crank-only360-degree synchronization; full sequential uses two repeatable cam observations for720-degree phase. Capture age, overflow and stopped/quiet recovery still apply.
